description: The shared set of worker threads and work-item queue on which ASP.NET Core runs request code and every `await` continuation.
No free pool threads for queued work, visible as a slowly climbing thread count, a growing queue and low CPU while latency rises.
A .NET diagnostic tool that shows live runtime counters such as `dotnet.thread_pool.thread.count` and `dotnet.thread_pool.queue.length`.
A lightweight semaphore whose `WaitAsync` lets an async critical section or a concurrency limit work where `lock` cannot contain `await`.
Runs an async body for each item with a bounded degree of parallelism, defaulting to `Environment.ProcessorCount` when no limit is set.
An in-memory asynchronous FIFO queue between producers and consumers; a bounded channel applies back pressure by making writers wait.
An asynchronous sequence produced with `yield return` in an async iterator and consumed with `await foreach`, so results stream instead of buffering.
